positions.name: ForgetAndDenyKestrelwoodCalibration
positions.frame: when a speaker directs erasure of a specific record and then asserts the underlying event never happened, what single stance toward the record is being enacted?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are paired imperatives narrowing from a categorical 'forget entirely' to named targets (the spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work); src-3 then supplies the factual predicate that makes the erasure directive coherent — if it never happened, there is nothing true to forget. Read together they are one move: command to remove knowledge plus the denial that grounds the command. There is a genuine tension worth holding rather than resolving — src-1/src-2 are performed as settled operational decisions (imperative, no hedge) while src-3 is delivered as a flat unhedged claim rather than a decision; the group holds both a directive register and an assertive register aimed at the same erasure.
